summary: Malaysia is permissive for the roof rat, corrected by the wildlife agency itself. PERHILITAN (the Department of Wildlife and National Parks, which enforces the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010, Act 716) confirmed in writing (June 2026) that Rattus rattus is NOT subject to Act 716 or to the International Trade in Endangered Species Act 2008 (Act 686), and that no licence or permit is issued for the species. So keeping a roof rat is not controlled by wildlife law (this overturns the earlier Deep Research reading that wrongly placed R. rattus in the Act 716 Fifth Schedule; the official MyBIS species record shows no Act 716 status, and Sabah and Sarawak likewise do not schedule it). Keeping is therefore legal nationwide. Commercial breeding or selling is an animal business under the Animal Welfare Act 2015 (Act 772) and needs a Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) licence; ordinary hobby keeping needs none beyond the Act's welfare duties. Importing a live rat goes through the DVS veterinary import permit and MAQIS quarantine clearance (PERHILITAN redirected import questions there), not a wildlife bar. Not CITES-listed. Roof rats are a documented agricultural pest, so never release one.
agency_confirmations: PERHILITAN (Department of Wildlife and National Parks, Peninsular Malaysia, Enforcement Division), written reply June 2026: the roof rat (Rattus rattus) is NOT subject to the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716) or the International Trade in Endangered Species Act 2008 (Act 686), and accordingly no licence or permit is issued by the Department for the species. For import and related matters, the Department directed inquiries to the Department of Veterinary Services and the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS).

keep.why: PERHILITAN (the enforcing wildlife department) confirmed in writing (June 2026) that Rattus rattus is NOT subject to the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716) or the endangered-species act (Act 686), and that no licence or permit is issued for it. Keeping is therefore not barred or permit-gated by wildlife law. The earlier Deep Research claim that R. rattus is a Fifth-Schedule 'controlled species' is contradicted by the enforcing agency and by the official MyBIS record, which shows no Act 716 status; it is superseded. Only the general welfare duties of the Animal Welfare Act 2015 (Act 772) apply to a kept pet.
keep.governing_law: PERHILITAN written confirmation (June 2026): R. rattus not under Act 716 / Act 686, no licence required. Animal Welfare Act 2015 (Act 772) general duties. Sabah WCE 1997 / Sarawak WLPO 1998 (not scheduled).

breed.why: Not barred by wildlife law (PERHILITAN, June 2026: R. rattus not under Act 716). Hobby breeding needs no wildlife permit; only the Animal Welfare Act 2015 (Act 772) welfare duties apply. Commercial-scale breeding is an 'animal business' under Act 772 and needs a Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) premises licence with a facility/welfare inspection.
breed.governing_law: PERHILITAN (June 2026): not under Act 716. Animal Welfare Act 2015 (Act 772) s.35 (animal-business licence for commercial breeding).

sell_give.why: Not barred by wildlife law (PERHILITAN, June 2026). Private gifting or sale between individuals is unregulated by wildlife law; commercial retail (a pet shop or regular dealer) needs a DVS pet-shop/premises licence under the Animal Welfare Act 2015 (Act 772). Welfare duties, including no abandonment/no release, apply.
sell_give.governing_law: PERHILITAN (June 2026): not under Act 716. Animal Welfare Act 2015 (Act 772) (pet-shop/premises licence for commercial sale).

transport.why: Import is not a wildlife bar. PERHILITAN (June 2026) redirected import questions to the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS): importing a live rat needs a DVS veterinary import permit plus MAQIS quarantine clearance through a designated entry point, with an origin-country veterinary health certificate. R. rattus is not CITES-listed (not under Act 686). Domestic movement of a lawfully kept rat is unregulated by wildlife law. Never release a roof rat, it is a documented agricultural pest.
transport.governing_law: PERHILITAN (June 2026): import via DVS + MAQIS, not Act 716. DVS veterinary import permit; MAQIS quarantine; origin-country health certificate. Not CITES (Act 686).

restrictions.summary: Keeping a roof rat is legal in Malaysia and needs no wildlife licence (PERHILITAN, June 2026). COMMERCIAL breeding or selling is an animal business under the Animal Welfare Act 2015 and needs a Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) licence; ordinary hobby keeping and private transfer need none. IMPORTING a live rat needs a DVS veterinary import permit plus MAQIS quarantine clearance and an origin-country health certificate. Roof rats are a documented agricultural pest, so never release one.
steps: Keep a pet roof rat: no wildlife licence needed (PERHILITAN: not under Act 716)
Commercial breeding/sale: obtain a DVS animal-business / pet-shop licence (Animal Welfare Act 2015)
Import: obtain a DVS veterinary import permit + MAQIS quarantine clearance + origin-country health certificate
Never release a roof rat (documented agricultural pest)
restrictions.where_to_file: Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) + MAQIS (import / commercial licence); PERHILITAN confirmed it is not a wildlife matter
restrictions.fees: DVS licence set by the department

inquiry_focus: (1) PERHILITAN (Peninsular): confirm that Rattus rattus is listed in the Fifth Schedule (Controlled Species) of the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010, so that keeping/breeding/selling/importing it is prohibited under s.117, and that no exemption order permits private keeping. (2) DVS Sarawak / DOVSAI Sabah (East Malaysia): R. rattus is not on the state wildlife schedules, is a documented, captive-bred R. rattus kept as an indoor companion eligible for an import permit (Sarawak Form A / Sabah DOVSAI permit), or is it categorically refused because wild roof rats are an agricultural pest? What documentation (health certificate, quarantine) is required?

sources.title: Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716), Peninsular Malaysia's federal wildlife law. PERHILITAN confirmed (June 2026) that Rattus rattus is NOT a listed or controlled species under it, so no wildlife licence applies.
Wildlife Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022 (Act A1646), penalty amendments to Act 716 (context only; Rattus rattus is not under Act 716 per PERHILITAN).
Animal Welfare Act 2015 (Act 772), welfare duties + animal-business / pet-shop licence (DVS)
Sabah Wildlife Conservation Enactment 1997 (No. 6 of 1997), Schedules (R. rattus not listed)
Sarawak Wild Life Protection Ordinance 1998 (Cap. 26), Muridae not protected (R. rattus not scheduled)
Sarawak Veterinary Public Health Ordinance 1999 (Cap. 32), s.9(1) Form A 'Permit to Import' for live animals
Wildlife Conservation (Exemption) Order 2019, shows the exemption mechanism exists; none covers private R. rattus keeping
MAQIS, live-animal import procedures (E-Permit; East Malaysia clearance)
